messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing a noisy Xid 13/31 spike in eu-west1 A10 pool starting ~20:12 UTC. appears correlated with an embedder tenant traffic shift to smaller batch sizes. putting logs here to help triage.

maria: dmesg snippet:
```
[1345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13) 0x00000000 at 0x7ff... channel 4c
[1345.678905] NVRM: Xid (31) 0x00000000 channel 4c fault
[1346.001234] gpu0: ECC recovered errors: +23
```

junaid: can you dump a host-level histogram? want counts by host and by card. quick query I usually run: 
```
SELECT host, gpu_id, count(*) FROM gpu_xid WHERE xid IN (13,31) AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY host, gpu_id ORDER BY count DESC;
```

cory: saw related soft-drains around 20:10 for host gpu-az3-148. card0 had ECC jump and we moved a few tenants off. rack euw-a10-rack7 looks noisy.

lei: quick hypothesis — small batch + high concurrency might be thrashing KV/cache or causing frequent PCIe refills. In our runtime that can surface as memory/driver faults (Xid 13/31). Repro idea: run same tenant traffic at batchshape (1,1) vs (8,1) and watch Xid.

ops-bot: ALERT: 3 Xid13 events detected on euw-a10-rack7 in last 10m. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xaXid?panelId=7 (auto-alert)

sre-oncall: proposed triage plan:
1) soft-drain affected card(s) (non-disruptive)
2) repro in staging with identical tenant-weighted request stream
3) if repro stable, schedule replacement on next maintenance window and mark card for vendor RMA
4) temporary routing: move critical tenants to h100-fallback pool + enable reduced batching for embedder until resolved
5) capture full kernel + nvidia-smi pmon while repro runs

junaid: running repro now against test-tenant (generator). script i run: 
```
# simple load generator
for s in {1..600}; do
  python load_gen.py --tenant test-tenant --batch 1 --seq-len 512 --qps 50 &
  sleep 0.5
done
```

maria: thanks. starting soft-drain for gpu-az3-148/0 (softdrain --> true, route traffic off gradually). moving 4 embedder tenants to h100-fallback. will snapshot /var/log/kern.log and nvidia pmon for 30m. :thumbsup:

cory: note — we rolled driver 530->535 in euw last week. any overlap between driver rollout and these hosts? if repro doesn't reproduce, we should check driver regressions and PCIe link flaps. also check pcie link state changes in dmesg.

lei: also add latency correlation: if Xid spikes align with tail latency >200ms or queue depth jumps, that points to queuing/backpressure rather than pure HW fault. do a 1m rolling join of xid events to tail latency.

maria: agreed — junaid can you produce a 1m join: xid count vs p95/p99 for that tenant? if we see p99 jump before xid, that supports thrash hypothesis.

junaid: on it. preliminary numbers (first 5m): hosts with Xid have p99 ~340ms vs baseline 120ms. pushing full graph now.

sre-oncall: next actions: (A) keep soft-drain in place until end of repro run (B) if repro produces >10 Xid events in 30m, escalate to replace card (C) open RMA ticket + schedule swap with hw-ops. tagging owners: @maria @junaid @cory.

maria: will update thread in 15m with logs and metric links. if we confirm HW, swap and label card as flaky. otherwise we can try reverting driver on one host for an A/B test.

cory: also capturing pmon counters and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 10` during repro. will paste outputs if anything jumps.

lei: nice. if we end up with no repro but persistent noise, consider isolating tenants with highest small-batch rates to dedicated low-latency hosts (policy change) as a mitigation.

maria: ack. starting ticket: INFRA-4621 (gpu fuzz Xid triage) and adding checklist. will post updates here.
